title.narrative: Identifying market opportunities for Small Scale Farmers in Zambia

description.narrative: The problem: 80% of Zambians depend on land for their livelihood. Of these, 60% are farmers with less than 3 hectares of land. These small-scale farmers generally produce limited quantities of vegetables and fruit but have great difficulty in accessing profitable markets for this produce and remain in poverty. International experience shows that farmers who grow and market horticultural products earn more income than cereal or pulse growers. However, for this potential to be realised, these growers need ready and efficient access to markets. For Zambian small-scale farmers, this is particularly difficult: barriers include scale of operation, insufficient knowledge of standards and related skills. What we will do: Identify market opportunities for fresh produce suited to Zambia's agronomic conditions. Evaluate farmers' capacities to grow these crops and to develop sustainable businesses to link the farmers to identified markets. Evaluate target communities commitment and buy-in to participate in interventions linking them to identified markets. Establish commitment of integrators to source from identified communities and explore sustainable procurement and business models. The result: Delivery of a business plan linking farmers to identified markets and provide for capacity building interventions to strengthen the farmers' participation in the supply chain.
